title: When the Wolf Turns
premise: In the drowned kingdom of Vessia, Theo Halloran keeps ledgers for the Mnemosyne Guild, which buys, sells, and erases memories for those who can afford to forget. When the crown declares a purge of all memory-thieves, Theo learns his own ledger holds proof that he unknowingly stole a memory from the dead queen—the location of a door out of Vessia, a country being erased from maps and minds alike. Hunted by the guild's enforcer and by soldiers who burn what they cannot tax, Theo must trade away pieces of himself to buy passage, until only one memory remains: the truth of who he was before the guild found him. In the end he opens the door and steps through, but chooses to leave the ledger behind so no one else can be bought or sold—paying for survival with everything except himself.
about_author: Orsen Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city's municipal records. They write fantasy about bureaucracies of the impossible, where magic is always someone's property.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He balances the guild's ledgers by candlelight, cataloguing memories like currency—a general's cowardice, a widow's first love—while hiding his own theft of a fragment belonging to the dead queen. The crown's proclamation arrives: all gifted persons are to be registered, then burned. Emotional beat: quiet dread as Theo realizes his invisibility was always an illusion the guild sold him.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with interludes from the memories themselves. Fleeing the guildhouse as enforcers raze it, Theo deciphers the queen's stolen fragment: coordinates to a door that exists only while her name is still spoken somewhere. The guildmaster, half-mad from eating his own inventory, offers Theo freedom in exchange for the fragment. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal as Theo understands the guild built its fortune on people exactly like him.

chapters.title: A Country Being Unmade
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Theo and Captain Ilsa Vey, the hunter ordered to burn the gifted but secretly carrying a purchased memory of her dead brother. Their paths converge at the flooded cathedral where the door stands. Theo must spend his own memories—one per ward—to keep the door's approach open, forgetting his mother's face, his first theft, his name. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve; Ilsa begins to doubt her crown.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Turns
chapters.summary: Theo and Ilsa POV. At the threshold, the guildmaster arrives with soldiers, demanding the fragment; Ilsa turns against her orders, buying Theo time with her badge and blood. Theo spends his final memory—the truth of his origins—and opens the door as Vessia's name is spoken for the last time. He steps through alone, leaving the burning ledger behind. Emotional beat: bittersweet liberation; survival achieved, but paid for with selfhood, redeemed only by refusal to carry the trade forward.
